result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both boards keep all 14 tanks and ten columns on one screen, with the same warm, restrained serif-and-amber look that no longer reads as crypto. B does better on the alerts: FV4's 21.6 reading is coloured red and both problem rows get solid red warning pills and a left rule, while normal rows stay quiet. B's numbers and batch IDs also have stronger contrast. A dims its batch numbers and empty rows quite low, and its outlined alert pills are a little softer. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both keep all 14 tanks and ten columns on one screen in a similar warm, serif-led brewery style. A makes the alerts stronger: FV4 and FV7 get red row tints, filled red pills, a left accent bar, and FV4's 21.6 is shown in red. B uses fainter tints and outlined pills, does not mark the 21.6 reading, and has very small column headers and dim batch and brewer text, so it is a little harder to read at a glance.
